# Academic research — Medieval Soundspace in the New Digital Leisure Time Media

- Original source: [Academic research — Medieval Soundspace in the New Digital Leisure Time Media](https://repositori.udl.cat/bitstream/10459.1/56907/1/ImagoTemporis_2015n9p307.pdf)
- Author / publication: Juan Francisco Jiménez Alcázar and Gerardo Rodríguez / Imago Temporis. Medium Aevum IX
- Language / date: English; 2015, pp. 307–327; DOI 10.21001/itma.2015.9.14
- Access: Abstract and relevant PDF text inspected
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Format: original summary and research notes; not a transcript.

This scholarly article examines how game music and sound create recognizable ideas of the Middle Ages, rather than necessarily reconstructing historical sound accurately.

Robin Hood appears in footnote 26 on printed page 319. The authors cite a MeriStation review whose writer likes the period atmosphere of the music but switches it off. They use that example to emphasize the variability of individual listening experiences.

The paper adds a reception and medievalism perspective to the collection. Its Robin Hood reference is brief and based on another review; it is not an analysis of the game's audio files, musical score, or production process.
